name: mycrew
description: A harness for Claude Code, grouped by domain: primitives and house rules shared by everything, specialists who carry the work in each domain, a product plane with its task board, and the leadership that steers them. Install tools first.

plugins.name: tools
plugins.description: No domain of its own — small, project-agnostic skills you reach for mid-work, plus the house rule files every other plugin here builds on. Install this one first, whatever domain you're setting up.

plugins.name: programming-specialists
plugins.description: Layer 1/3 — the specialists, self-contained agents that know nothing of the management above them: coder, designer, devops, reviewer and tester, each with domain checklists as skills.

plugins.name: programming-product
plugins.description: Layer 2/3 — the product plane and its task board, both kept on backlog.md: what the whole product must do, and what is being done about it right now, plus the rule for working with code. /product-init stands it up.

plugins.name: programming-management
plugins.description: Layer 3/3 — the leadership of the product: a chief who is the human's deputy over the whole product, and a lead who holds one feature, each spawning specialists to carry the work. Management only: it never writes code.

plugins.name: copywriting-tools
plugins.description: Layer 1/2 — general-purpose writing components, usable standalone: two tone guides (tone-scientific, tone-conversational) for the author's registers, docx-build writes a Markdown-to-Word converter for one template out of shared modules, docx-verify proves the document is right by structure and by eye. excalidraw-export turns diagrams into PNG in the venue's font and warns when their text would print too small.

plugins.name: copywriting-specialists
plugins.description: Layer 2/2 — the specialists: a copywriter who writes any text from the material it is given, in the register the caller names or the material implies, a reviewer who checks facts, runs the AI-text detectors and says how the text lands, and a layouter who builds the Word document and proves every page renders. The three are peers and call each other. /article-init stands up an article's repository.
